verdict.headline: 2 things worth checking on this payslip

findings.title: This job is on a BR tax code
findings.explanation: BR means basic rate. Every pound you earn here is taxed at 20%, with none of your tax-free allowance applied to this job. That is correct if your £12,570 allowance is being used at another job. If this is your only income, or you have left the other job, you are probably paying tax you do not owe.

estimate.label: Possible overpayment so far this tax year

findings.next_step: Check your tax codes in your HMRC personal tax account, or ask your payroll team which job your allowance is applied to.

findings.title: No pension contributions on this payslip
findings.explanation: Nothing is going into a pension from this job. Auto-enrolment applies once you are 22 or over and earning above £10,000 a year from one employer, so this may simply mean you are not eligible yet. If you are eligible and opted out, you are also turning down whatever your employer would have added.
findings.next_step: Ask your employer whether you are eligible for auto-enrolment and what they contribute.

findings.title: National Insurance looks right
findings.explanation: You earn under the threshold where National Insurance starts, so nothing has been deducted. That is what we would expect.
